title: Copy-Then-Inpaint: Improving Temporal Consistency in Multi-Step GUI Generation via Selective Region Editing

contributions.purpose: Reduce temporal drift (compounding visual inconsistencies) in multi-step GUI trajectory generation.
contributions.mechanism: Copy-Then-Inpaint, a three-stage inference-time pipeline: a VLM predicts change-region bounding boxes for the current action, masked inpainting generates content only in those regions, and pixel-level compositing copies unchanged pixels from the previous frame.
contributions.evaluation: On GEBench Type 2 (n = 200) it significantly improves temporal consistency (CONS +5.7, p < 0.01) and overall quality (+6.1 GE-Score) without sacrificing task completion.
contributions.domain: GUI generation for autonomous agent training
contributions.source_quote: We propose Copy-Then-Inpaint, a simple yet effective pipeline for improving temporal consistency in multi-step GUI generation through selective region editing and pixel-level compositing.

contributions.purpose: Validate the pipeline's effectiveness on a standard GUI-generation benchmark.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluation on GEBench Type 2 against full-frame regeneration approaches with statistical testing.
contributions.evaluation: Significant improvement in temporal consistency (+5.7 CONS, p < 0.01) and overall quality (+6.1 GE-Score) without sacrificing task completion.
contributions.source_quote: We evaluate our method on GEBench Type 2, demonstrating significant improvement in temporal consistency (+5.7 CONS, p < 0.01) and overall quality (+6.1 GE-Score) without sacrificing task completion.

contributions.purpose: Identify which pipeline components drive the gains.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies on semantic mask alignment (shuffled masks) and mask dilation.
contributions.evaluation: Shuffled masks reduce gains by 4.0 CONS points and removing mask dilation hurts GOAL by 6.4 points, showing both components are necessary.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct ablation studies showing that semantic mask alignment is essential (shuffled masks reduce gains by 4.0 CONS points) and that mask dilation is necessary for task completion (removing it hurts GOAL by 6.4 points).

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work focuses on improving temporal consistency in multi-step GUI generation through selective region editing, complementing these approaches by addressing the temporal drift problem that arises when generating sequential frames.
Our approach adapts mask-based inpainting for GUI trajectory generation, using VLM-predicted change regions rather than user-provided or automatically detected masks.

Unlike these approaches that operate on natural images or videos, our method targets GUI environments where most actions modify only small regions. We leverage this domain-specific property through pixel-level compositing, which provides a simpler but effective mechanism for preserving unchanged regions across sequential frames.
